correctness.rationale: After quotienting by the kernel of the character, the problem is exactly an average over all L-th roots of unity. For L at least five, the quartic q majorizes the absolute positive trinomial pointwise and root-of-unity orthogonality gives its exact second and fourth moments, hence the 25/16 upper bound. Concavity gives the golden-ratio lower bound for the signed trinomial using the exact average of sin-squared. The cases L=3 and L=4 are evaluated directly. These arguments cover every admissible L and do not infer an infinite theorem from numerical testing.

originality.rationale: The closest located theorem, Krenedits 2010, proves the continuous-circle comparison for the same consecutive trinomial at p=1, while the present claim is an every-finite-cyclic-sampling statement with an explicit uniform gap. Bonami--Révész 2008 study finite cyclic L1 idempotent concentration but not signed majorant reversal. Krenedits describes a Mockenhaupt 1996 discrete uniform inequality in the different 2<p<4 and frequencies 1,3 regime, so that described statement does not imply the present one.

value.rationale: Three terms are the first possible idempotent size for Hardy--Littlewood majorant failure, making the consecutive arithmetic progression a canonical minimal object. Finite cyclic groups are independently motivated by the established ell-one idempotent concentration literature. The result gives an all-modulus persistence theorem with a uniform quantitative gap from a short moment certificate, rather than a small-N table or a routine reformulation of the continuous integral inequality.
